The batch therefore shifts toward missing early anchors and loading-qualified transitions in high-error nitrogen, carbonyl, and weak-eluent regions.","batch_rationale":"The batch repairs several measured failure regions while preserving local experimental meaning. The m119 pair tests a newly supported loading interaction; m73 receives one controlled reproducibility and loading check because recent repeats disagree with earlier records. The m160/m161 and m216 panels target nitrogen-rich rows with documented large underprediction, and the m200, m206, m90, and m13 selections probe nearby onset regimes rather than repeating already measured weak-eluent endpoints. The m181 loading and ratio panel, together with m98, m37, m166, m168, m203, m185, m184, and m114 anchors, covers carbonyl, lactone, aromatic, and halogenated boundaries where retention curves are nonlinear or endpoint-specific. Several matched loading pairs distinguish onset effects from completion effects. The remaining exploratory rows add coverage for less sampled aromatic structures and strong-eluent baselines. Together these labels should improve generalization by constraining structure-condition-retention relationships, repairing high-error tails, and identifying regions where deterministic transfer is unreliable."}
